review_candidates.title: Humanitarian Lead - Latin America and Caribbean region
review_candidates.description: Humanitarian Lead - Latin America and Caribbean region Permanent. Full Time. Hybrid working (2 days per week in the office) Location: Bogota, Colombia Salary: 181,256,397 Colombian Pesos per year If we receive a high volume of applications, we reserve the right to close the advert before the scheduled closing date. Therefore, we encourage interested applicants to apply at their earliest convenience. Applicants must already have the right to work in Colombia, and CV's and application forms should be in ENGLISH ONLY. About us Christian Aid exists to create a world where everyone can live a full life, free from poverty. We are a global movement of people, churches and local organisations who passionately champion dignity, equality and justice worldwide. We are the changemakers, the peacemakers, the mighty of heart. We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace, and recognise the value this brings in forming strong, creative and high performing teams. We welcome applications from all sections of the community, and from those with experience from outside of the voluntary sector. And no, you don’t have to be Christian to work here – we encourage people of all faiths and none to apply. We just ask that everyone lives out our values of dignity, equality, justice and love. We value a good work-life balance, so we’re open to part-time and flexible working. We also offer hybrid working for our office-based colleagues. About the role Reporting in to the Head of Impact, the Humanitarian Lead for the Latin America and Caribbean region will play a lead role in setting up new emergency programmes as well as managing existing emergency response programmes across Christian Aid programmes globally but with a primary focus on an agreed set of countries to maximise impact. In the Latin America and Caribbean region, Christian Aid operates in Colombia, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, and Haiti. The post-holder will will ensure Christian Aid’s people-centred humanitarian reform advocacy agenda is energetically communicated in relevant regional and country policy forums, so that the humanitarian sector regionally takes visible steps toward more people-centred and locally led humanitarian programming and aligns with organisational values and goals. Some of the key responsibilities of the role of Humanitarian Lead are: Manage and collaborate on new and existing humanitarian and emergency response programmes internally and externally to maximise impact. Manage staff and ensure they perform to a high standard, meeting their objectives with activities integrated with the Country Teams, aligning with organisational values and goals. Active engagement in Country Leadership Teams ensuring Christian Aid’s humanitarian mandate is integrated within the wider country strategies in line with “Standing Together”. Manage response strategies to ensure plans are in place, funding secured for humanitarian work with budget planning, monitoring and reporting in place ensuring the effective use of these funds and ensure they are high-impact initiatives to maximising impact. Deliver humanitarian programmes in a timely and accountable manner meeting the Core Humanitarian Standards (CHS), safeguarding, inclusion and other minimum standards, Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and resilience work, and ensuring high quality and maximising impact. Manage an active engagement in humanitarian programme policy advocacy work at national and international level feeding into the broader Christian Aid advocacy agenda around ongoing and crisis specific issues aligning to organisational values and goals. Manage our partners and ensure MCC staff are confident in, committed to and inspired by Christian Aid’s humanitarian signature focus on anticipatory action, cash transfer programming and survivor-led response to maximise impact. Deliver technical expertise through collaboration from within and outside Christian Aid is effectively engaged ensuring high quality programming. Collaborate and coordinate humanitarian programming within the relevant national and regional mechanisms, UNOCHA, clusters, ACT sisters and well recognised within donor and Civil Society circles and take advantage of opportunities to work harmoniously on humanitarian together programmes. About you Who we are looking for: Essential: Fluency in both Spanish and English (written and spoken) is required. University graduate or equivalent qualification. Significant knowledge of humanitarian issues and best practice in humanitarian action. Significant experience leading both rapid response and chronic emergencies or managing programmes to build resilient communities. Significant multi-country humanitarian programme support experience. Detailed understanding of the CHS, SPHERE and other humanitarian standards. Developed ability to equip and encourage staff to take responsibility and promote an empowered working. Developed ability to contribute to and work successfully as part of management and cross-organisational teams, with excellent time management and the ability to work with challenging deadlines and to multi task. Highly self-motivated with personal resilience. Highly developed communication skills in writing and oral, with a fluency in English. Developed ability to develop and maintain successful working relationships with a range of colleagues. Significant experience of emergency programme cycle management from needs assessment, through funding applications, management, review and evaluation. Desirable Developed skills in facilitation of learning and change processes. Management qualification. Experience of working with an NGO. Working knowledge of French is desirable, given the role's engagement with Haiti. Further information At Christian Aid we strive to be an inclusive and diverse employer and recognise the value that this brings in helping to build strong, creative and high performing teams. We are actively encouraging racialised minorities, LGBTQ+, people with disabilities, returning parents or carers who are re-entering work after a career break, people with caring responsibilities, people from low socioeconomic backgrounds, women, and older workers to apply. This is because these groups are under-represented within our teams, especially at senior level, and we recognise and value the contributions members of these groups make to strong, creative and high performing teams. We have a strong Christian ethos and we encourage applications from all faiths. Applicants will be expected to demonstrate an understanding of and sympathy with Christian Aid’s faith identity. All successful candidates will require a DBS/police check appropriate to the role and location and a Counter Terrorism Sanction check as part of your clearance for commencing your role with us. We also participate in the Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme . In line with this Scheme, we will request information as part of the referencing process from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures. This role requires applicants to have the right to live and work in the country where this position is based and undertake the role that you have been offered. If you are successful and we make you an offer for the role, we will be required to conduct a right to work check on your immigration status in the UK. We will contact you regarding the documentation you will need to provide to evidence this.

This role will be remote with national travel and ideally based in the Midlands/North. The HR Business Partner will act as a trusted adviser and coach to leaders, helping to develop management capability, strengthen leadership effectiveness and embed a culture of accountability, performance and continuous improvement. The role combines strategic business partnering with practical operational support, ensuring that people initiatives align with organisational objectives and contribute to improved business performance. As a key member of the Regional Leadership Team, you will influence decision-making, shape workforce strategies and lead the implementation of people initiatives that support growth, colleague engagement, service excellence and organisational effectiveness. Benefits for the role include Competitive Salary Annual car allowance Annual 10% Performance related bonus Private Healthcare 33 days annual leave (inclusive of bank holidays) with the option to purchase additional leave through salary sacrifice Life Assurance 24/7 online/telephone GP Consultation and access to prescriptions. 2nd opinion medical support following diagnosis or where a colleague is on a treatment pathway. Cash-plan benefits, providing colleagues the option of protecting themselves in case of illness and recuperation, including dental, optical, chiropody. Access to mental health and physiotherapy consultations. Access to legal advice on domestic issues e.g. motoring offences, wills and probate, and personal injury. Long Service Recognition Scheme – recognising colleagues for their continued service after 5 years and at 5-year intervals with an increase in annual leave. Role Responsibilities Partner with Regional Directors and leadership teams to develop and deliver regional people plans that support operational, commercial and organisational objectives. Provide strategic HR advice on business planning, organisational development, workforce transformation and growth. Ensure people considerations are embedded in regional decision-making and operational planning. Use workforce data, trends and insight to identify organisational risks, opportunities and targeted interventions. Lead and support organisational change, restructures, acquisitions, contract mobilisations and TUPE transfers. Coach, mentor and constructively challenge leaders to improve their confidence and effectiveness in managing people. Build capability in performance management, attendance, wellbeing, employee relations, talent development and colleague engagement. Identify leadership capability gaps and implement practical, measurable development solutions. Design and facilitate leadership workshops, management training and development interventions. Promote a culture in which managers take ownership and accountability for leading, developing and engaging their teams. Provide expert guidance on complex employee relations matters, ensuring compliance with employment legislation, organisational policy and good practice. Work collaboratively with specialist People colleagues to mitigate legal, employee relations, financial and reputational risk. Lead and support workforce planning, succession planning and talent management activity across the region. Drive colleague engagement activity and ensure feedback is translated into clear and meaningful action. Help embed a positive, inclusive and high-performance culture aligned with EMED values and behaviours. Build credible and productive relationships with operational leaders, senior stakeholders, employee representatives and trade unions. Influence decisions at senior level through clear advice, professional expertise and constructive challenge. Represent the People Function at Regional Leadership Team meetings and operational forums. Support client presentations, bids, contract mobilisations and business development activity where appropriate. This role supports a geographically dispersed operational workforce and requires a significant and consistent regional presence. The successful candidate will: Travel regularly throughout the designated region to support operational locations and management teams. Spend time in operational environments to understand local challenges and identify effective people solutions. Attend regional and national meetings, leadership events, workshops and project activity. Undertake occasional overnight stays where business needs require. Success in the role will be assessed through agreed objectives and measures, including: Delivery and impact of regional people plans. Do you have what it takes? CIPD Level 5 qualification or above, or equivalent professional experience. Significant experience operating as an HR Business Partner within a complex, multi-site organisation. A proven record of strategic business partnering with senior operational leaders. Strong coaching and leadership development experience, with evidence of building management capability. Extensive knowledge of UK employment law and employee relations practice. Experience of leading and supporting organisational change and transformation. Demonstrable commercial awareness and the ability to connect people priorities with business outcomes. Experience of working in a unionised environment. Excellent communication, influencing and stakeholder management skills. The ability to interpret people data and turn insight into practical, targeted action. Desirable Chartered CIPD membership. Experience within healthcare, emergency services, logistics, transport or another operationally intensive sector. Experience supporting large, geographically dispersed workforces. Experience of TUPE transfers, bids and contract mobilisation activity. About Us EMED Group is an established healthcare logistics provider that enables access to health and social care through our four specialist divisions. We are one of the largest health and care partners to the NHS with 4,000 colleagues across over 60 bases UK-wide. EMED Group is committed to pro-actively improving the wellbeing of our communities by providing access to vital health and social care services across the UK.

review_candidates.title: Head of Operational Support
review_candidates.description: Background: The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation dedicated to protecting the rights of displaced and affected people during crises. NRC delivers high-quality programmes to support people forced to flee, helping them rebuild their lives and establish a new future. NRC provides immediate humanitarian assistance, prevents further displacement, and contributes to durable solutions. It operates across both new and protracted crises across 40 countries. The country programmes in the East and Southern Africa region incorporate Ethiopia, Uganda, South Sudan, Sudan, Somalia, Kenya, and Mozambique. NRC exited from Tanzania in 2026. NRC has a simplified organisational structure with a leaner Head Office in Oslo and Representation Offices and smaller Regional Teams. Global support structures are established for functions previously managed by the Regional Offices, including Finance, Risk & Compliance, People & Organisation, Media and Communication, PCM & Grants Management. The Regional Team and Country Offices will access support capacity from these Global Resource Pools. Resource Pools (hereafter pool) gather staff in one common team which is organised and managed (but not necessarily physically located) at Head Office. The purpose of pooling is to improve efficiency, equity, access and flexibility. The teams should ensure predictable access to the same services and deliver them in an efficient way. In Nairobi Kenya, several members of the different pools are physically located in the regional office, the Regional Head of Operational Support ensures streamlining of hosting arrangements and a conducive working environment for all. What we are looking for: The Regional Head of Operational Support will ensure an integrated approach to operational management, supporting the quality and timeliness of NRC's response in the region. The role is responsible for enabling support needs in countries across HR, Risk and Compliance, Humanitarian Access and Safety (HAS), Finance, ICT, Logistics and Administration, ensuring compliance with NRC policies. The Regional Head of Operational Support plays a crucial role in ensuring that the region is accountable for the performance of country offices, ensuring they meet operational standards and deliver on strategic objectives. The role ensures a conducive working environment for all teams, including members of different global teams physically located in the regional office in Nairobi. This role is a member of the Regional Management Team and the Global Support Advisory Group (GSAG) led by the deputy SG/ CFO. What you will do: Ensure that support functions within the regional team operate efficiently, fostering a collaborative and effective working environment. Hold country offices accountable for progress on their operations by leveraging reports, analyses, and compliance data from NRC’s global resource and pools. Support country directors and heads of support, HAS Managers with capacity building and problem-solving related to operational challenges. Provide advice and mentorship to country office operational support teams, fostering capacity building and skills development. Participate in global discussions on planning and strategy relating to support functions. Review of finance, HR and logistics requirements related to regional grants in collaboration with the Global PCM and Grants Management facility. Streamline the hosting arrangements for members of global pools physically located in the regional office and ensure a conducive working environment The postholder, upon request, can act on behalf of the Regional Director including leading relevant Crisis Management Teams. Note: The above responsibilities are just a snapshot. Hence, please refer to the full job description for you to have a full understanding. What you will bring: 1. Professional competencies Minimum 10 years of relevant leadership/management experience within the humanitarian field Relevant higher education in a related field such as business administration, management, finance or other suitable education Background and experience in managing support functions: finance, HR and logistics. It is an added value to have experience from working with security and safety Experience from working in complex and volatile contexts Documented/proven results related to the position’s responsibilities Relevant experience with overseeing Finance, Logistics or other support functions will be an asset. Knowledge about own leadership skills/profile Fluency in English, both written and verbal 2. Context related skills, knowledge and experience: Essential: Fluency in English both written and verbal Knowledge of the context in East and Southern Africa is an asset. Experience with start-ups, exit and organisational change processes Ability to collaborate effectively with remote teams and stakeholders 3. Behavioural competencies: Build meaningful relations I communicate clearly and transparently I treat all people with respect I work collaboratively with partners and internal stakeholders Act with integrity I base my action and good judgement assuring necessary change I act as a role model for our principles and values Empower people I delegate and give feedback that allows people to grow I set clear expectations and direction I challenge and support my team to accomplish shared goals Deliver results I always look for the best solution for the people we serve I prioritize and plan enabling my team to achieve results I am accountable and take responsibility for my actions and our results What we offer: Duty station: Nairobi, Kenya Salary/benefits: grade 11 on NRC’s either international or national salary scale. Duration of Contract: 2 years, national. Or international with full family package. NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability. We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative. Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC Important information about the application process: For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity MarketPlace. When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education. Applicants who do not fill in the required information will not be considered for the role. Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV. Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered. Mandatory to submit the below when applying: Your most updated English CV and remove all previous outdated CVs. English Cover Letter Do not attach certificates or any other documents apart from the two mentioned above. Incomplete applications or the ones submitted in other languages than English will not be considered. This position is open for international and national candidates. We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. If you have any questions about this role, please email esa.recruitment@nrc.no with the job title as the subject line. Why NRC? The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year. Watch this short video to see NRC in action. We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to: Do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts. Join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility. Be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity. Learn more about NRC

review_candidates.description: Är du redo för en större uppgift? Polismyndigheten är Sveriges största myndighet med ca 40 700 medarbetare över hela landet. Hos oss får du möjlighet att bidra till Polisens uppdrag – att öka tryggheten och minska brottsligheten i samhället. Organisation Nationella operativa avdelningen Kommun Malmö Län Skåne län Utlyst 22 september 2026 Ansök senast 6 oktober 2026 Referensnummer A573.270/2026 Arbetsplatsbeskrivning Nationella operativa avdelningen (Noa) ansvarar för att stärka hela Polismyndigheten genom att driva utveckling och upprätthålla en strategisk nationell lägesbild över brottsligheten. Vidare samordnar Noa nationellt och internationellt arbete för brottsbekämpande verksamhet samt högspecialiserad och unik polisverksamhet som kompletterar polisregionerna vid behov. Nationella gränspolisenheten har nationellt ansvar för gränspolisverksamheten och ansvarar för att samordna, strukturera, stödja och metodutveckla polisens arbete med gränskontroll, inre utlänningskontroll och verkställigheter. Enheten är nationell kontaktpunkt för EU:s gräns- och kustbevakningsbyrå Frontex och samordnar Sveriges deltagande i byråns gränskontroll- och gemensamma återvändandeoperationer. Sektionen för gränssamordning ansvarar för den nationella samordningscentralen, NCC, och gruppen för Etias. NCC består av medarbetare från Polismyndigheten, Tullverket och Kustbevakningen. Varje medlemsstat har ett NCC där arbetet genomförs inom ramarna för Eurosur. NCC:s huvudsakliga uppgift är att upprätthålla den nationella och den europeiska situationsbilden samt fungera som nationell kontaktpunkt i frågor som rör svensk gräns. Det handlar bland annat om migration, rörelser som sker inom Schengenområdet samt internationella brottsnätverk verksamma i såväl Sverige som i vårt närområde. Sektionen består av fyra grupper: NCC Situationsbild, NCC Analys och NCC Samordning, sektionens fjärde grupp är under uppbyggnad och kommer att hantera EU:s digitala inresetillstånd Etias. Genom Etiasförordningen åläggs samtliga EU-medlemsstater att inrätta en nationell Etias-enhet. Medborgare från omkring 60 viseringsfria länder kommer när Etias tagits i drift att behöva ansöka om resetillstånd innan avresa till Schengen. Arbetsbeskrivning Vi söker nu handläggare till den nya nationella gruppen Etias som ska arbeta med det EU-gemensamma systemet för reseuppgifter och resetillstånd. Gruppen är placerad vid sektionen för gränssamordning med placering i Malmö. Huvuduppgiften kommer vara att utreda, riskbedöma och fatta beslut i ansökningar om resetillstånd. Vid hanteringen av ansökningar kommer det krävas samordning med andra länder, Europol, ett flertal myndigheter i Sverige och andra funktioner inom Polismyndigheten. Därtill kommer gruppen bl.a. att hantera överklaganden och företräda myndigheten i domstol i resetillståndsärenden, fatta beslut om att ogiltigförklara och återkalla resetillstånd samt hantera dataskyddsrelaterade förfrågningar inom ramen för Etias. Handläggningen av resetillståndsärenden sker i enlighet med Etiasförordningen och den svenska förvaltningslagen. Den nationella Etias-enheten kommer att vara den funktion som ansvarar för Etias-verksamheten både nationellt och internationellt för Sveriges räkning. You might currently work in philanthropy, government, diplomacy, an international institution, business or civil society. You may already work in climate, but you don't necessarily need to. Turn ideas into action , developing clear theories of change, pathways to impact, resource plans and fundable propositions.  Establish CECG in new international spaces , building our credibility and presence beyond our existing programmatic footprint.  Lead strategy execution , overseeing programme teams, grant-making portfolios, budgets, monitoring, evaluation and learning. Established senior networks within areas such as trade, international finance, global security, the G20/G7 or regional institutions and groupings.  Demonstrable experience of developing and leading strategies that have delivered meaningful impact.  Strong experience of working in and with the Global South, including established professional networks.
